carriers.doc: The request handed to the model.
State handed to an agent invocation.

A turn of the request a model call received, in the request's order. ADK for Go writes the whole request as events at request time, so a later trace re-sends an earlier trace's turns under the later trace's time: the replay is recognised by its place in the replayed prefix, never by its time. Each event is one message of the request, so two at different places are two messages - as in `llm_request`, which lists the same request: ADK quotes every earlier agent step behind the same preamble, and read as one occurrence that preamble's copies would be matched to the wrong messages of the other carrier.
The model's own output, one emission per call.
The choice that ends the model's output without a piece of it: the same emission as the choices before it.

detect.doc: Ranked ahead of every service-name fallback: ADK's own attributes are conclusive.
detect.label: GoogleADK

messages.doc: Every carrier this dialect writes a conversation to, with the local order between them: the tool-call arguments are read only when the request payload supplied nothing, which is what the code being replaced expressed as a `!found` check.

primary.doc: The request. Its members arrive under two spellings - the native Vertex form in camelCase and this framework's own in snake_case under `config` - so each reading lists both. An empty object is not a request.

also.doc: The system instruction: structured parts, a bare string, or the framework's own snake_case member.
The same instruction written as a string.

The conversation. Gemini writes `{parts, role}`, so the role comes from the payload rather than a literal - one rule per role would be the alternative. Read structurally so the provider's payload is cloned unchanged; see the projection-language section of `docs/engineering/framework-rules-engine.md` for why.

primary.doc: The tools the request was given, as one observation - a set, not a sequence of turns. Prefer the top-level list, else the nested one; each group either wraps its declarations under one of two spellings or is a declaration itself.

fallback_if_primary_empty.doc: A tool call's arguments, read only when the request payload supplied nothing.

always.doc: The response. `model` is this provider's name for the assistant, normalised here so the alias sits beside the dialect that uses it; the reason a turn stopped is reported beside the content rather than inside it, and lower-cased to the canonical form.
The conversation handed to an agent. Neither an empty object nor an empty list is a conversation.

messages.doc: ADK for Go writes every turn of a model request as a semantic-convention event whose `content` is the model API's whole message - `{role, parts}` - and names every non-system turn `gen_ai.user.message`, the model's own replies included. The message is read as it stands, so its stated role decides (a replayed `model` turn is the assistant's) and its parts are content blocks; the event's raw form keeps only what this reading leaves, which is no content at all. Gated on ADK's instrumentation scope, because the tag's carrier declares ADK's replay timing, and on the shape, so a `content` that is text or any other object is the event's ordinary member.

alternatives.doc: The model API's own message: a role and its parts.

messages.doc: A chunk of a streamed response: ADK for Python writes a `gen_ai.choice` for every response its model adapter yields until one states a finish reason, so the ones before it are pieces of that answer, never answers of their own. A function call in one is a call of the answer unless Gemini marks it as still arriving.

partial_calls.doc: A function call streamed in pieces carries the streaming members, as ADK itself tells one (`streaming_utils`): `partial_args`, even empty - the Interactions adapter opens a call with an empty list before its arguments arrive - or `will_continue`, true while more follows and false or absent on the closing piece. A call with neither is whole.

alternatives.doc: The model API's own message, as the terminal choice writes it.

messages.doc: The model's answer as ADK reports it: a `gen_ai.choice` whose `content` is the model API's message, with the finish reason the event states beside it. Read like the request turns, under a tag of its own because it is the call's output rather than its input. The choice that states a finish reason ends a response ADK for Python may have streamed in chunks before it (`google-adk.event_choice_chunk`), and what it holds depends on the model adapter: the whole answer through LiteLLM, which aggregates; only the last chunk through Gemini's own adapter, whose aggregate ADK never records. So the terminal is `unknown`, resolved by the response ADK's `call_llm` step recorded around the call.

alternatives.doc: The model API's own message: a role and its parts.

lift.doc: The reason the model stopped, which the event states beside its content.

messages.doc: A choice that only ends a streamed response: Gemini's last chunk may state the finish reason and carry no content, which ADK's exporter writes as a `content` member with no value, so the event has none. It holds no piece of the answer, so it is a `delta`: the answer is the chunks before it, joined, and what this says is why the model stopped. Tagged apart from `google_adk.choice_content`, whose carrier it does not read.

span_facts.doc: A tool's response is recorded only on the span that ran it.

provider_aliases.doc: This framework names itself in `gen_ai.system`, and its models are served by a provider the catalogue prices - so the value has to resolve to that provider or every one of its calls is priced from the model name alone. Declared here, in the asset that owns the framework, rather than beside the catalogue's own provider spellings.

The same value with no separator, which is how one exporter writes it. Both spellings, because normalisation replaces `-` and a space with `_` rather than removing them - so this is a different value, not a variant of the one above.
